content: The references provided are a comprehensive list of studies, reviews, and guidelines related to tuberculosis (TB), particularly focusing on drug-resistant TB, pediatric TB, and TB-HIV co-infection. 1. Seddon JA, Hesseling AC, Godfrey-Faussett P, Schaaf HS conducted an observational cohort study published in Thorax in 2014, which demonstrated high treatment success rates in children treated for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). The study provided critical insights into the effectiveness of treatment regimens for pediatric MDR-TB. 2. Shah NS, Yuen CM, Heo M, et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014, to evaluate the yield of contact investigations in households of patients with drug-resistant TB. This study highlighted the importance of contact tracing in identifying additional cases of TB. 3. Ettehad D, Schaaf HS, Seddon JA, et al. published a systematic review and meta-analysis in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2012, focusing on treatment outcomes for children with MDR-TB. The findings emphasized the challenges and potential strategies for improving pediatric MDR-TB management. 4. Gegia M, Jenkins HE, Kalandadze I, Furin J reported on the outcomes of children treated for TB with second-line medications in Georgia between 2009 and 2011. Published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013, the study provided valuable data on the efficacy of second-line TB drugs in resource-limited settings. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) released consolidated guidelines on TB treatment, specifically addressing drug-resistant TB treatment in Module 4. These guidelines, accessed in December 2021, provide evidence-based recommendations for managing drug-resistant TB globally. 6. Dooley KE, Rosenkranz SL, Conradie F, et al. conducted a phase 2, open-label, randomized controlled trial published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2021. The study investigated the QT effects of bedaquiline, delamanid, or their combination in patients with rifampicin-resistant TB, offering critical safety data for these drugs. 7. Svensson EM, Aweeka F, Park JG, et al. used model-based estimates to study the effects of efavirenz on bedaquiline pharmacokinetics and suggested dose adjustments for patients co-infected with HIV and TB. This study, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2013, provided guidance for optimizing co-treatment regimens. 8. Svensson EM, Dooley KE, Karlsson MO explored the impact of lopinavir-ritonavir or nevirapine on bedaquiline exposures in TB-HIV co-infected patients. Published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2014, the study highlighted potential drug-drug interactions and their implications for treatment. 9. Brill MJ, Svensson EM, Pandie M, et al. confirmed model-predicted pharmacokinetic interactions between bedaquiline and lopinavir/ritonavir or nevirapine in patients with HIV and drug-resistant TB. This study, published in The International Journal of Antimicrobial Agents in 2017, reinforced the need for careful consideration of drug interactions in co-infected patients. 10. Mallikaarjun S, Wells C, Petersen C, et al. demonstrated that delamanid co-administered with antiretroviral or anti-TB drugs showed no clinically relevant drug-drug interactions in healthy subjects. Published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2016, this study supported the safety of delamanid in combination therapies. 11. The Stop TB Partnership Global Drug Facility Pediatric Drug-Resistant TB Donation Initiative, detailed on the Sentinel Project website in 2019, aimed to improve access to pediatric formulations of drug-resistant TB medications. 12. Svensson EM, du Bois J, Kitshoff R, et al. investigated the relative bioavailability of bedaquiline tablets suspended in water, with implications for dosing in children. Published in British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology in 2018, the study provided practical guidance for pediatric TB treatment. 13. Schaaf HS, Thee S, van der Laan L, et al. reviewed adverse effects of oral second-line anti-TB drugs in children. Published in Expert Opinion on Drug Safety in 2016, the study highlighted the safety profile of these medications in pediatric populations. 14. Garcia-Prats AJ, Schaaf HS, Hesseling AC reviewed the safety and tolerability of second-line injectable anti-TB drugs in children. Published in Expert Opinion on Drug Safety in 2016, the study provided critical insights into the risks associated with these treatments. 15. Schaaf HS, Garcia-Prats AJ, McKenna L, Seddon JA discussed the challenges of using new and repurposed drugs for treating MDR-TB in children. Published in Expert Review of Clinical Pharmacology in 2018, the article emphasized the need for innovative approaches to pediatric TB care. 16. Garcia-Prats AJ, Schaaf HS, Draper HR, et al. combined data from two prospective observational studies to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, optimal dosing, and safety of linezolid in children with MDR-TB. Published in PLOS Medicine in 2019, the study provided evidence for the use of linezolid in pediatric TB treatment. 17. The WHO operational handbook on TB, Module 5, focuses on the management of TB in children and adolescents. This resource, accessed in December 2021, provides comprehensive guidance for healthcare providers. 18. Isaakidis P, Paryani R, Khan S, et al. reported poor outcomes in a cohort of HIV-infected adolescents undergoing treatment for MDR-TB in Mumbai, India. Published in PLOS One in 2013, the study underscored the challenges of managing co-infections in resource-limited settings. 19. Moyo S, Furin JJ, Hughes J, et al. examined outcomes in adolescents treated for drug-resistant TB in Cape Town, South Africa, between 2008 and 2013. Published in Archives of Pediatric Infectious Diseases in 2015, the study highlighted the need for targeted interventions in this age group. 20. A family-centered approach to the treatment and prevention of drug-resistant TB in children and adolescents was detailed in a counseling tool accessed in March 2022. This resource emphasized the importance of family involvement in TB care. 21. Allwood BW, Byrne A, Meghji J, et al. reviewed post-TB lung disease as an under-recognized global challenge. Published in Respiration in 2021, the article called for increased awareness and management of long-term TB sequelae. 22. Allwood BW, Amaral AFS, Byrne A, et al. discussed perspectives on post-TB lung health from the First International Symposium. Published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2020, the article highlighted the importance of addressing post-TB complications. 23. Dodd PJ, Yuen CM, Jayasooriya SM, et al. quantified the global number of TB survivors in a modeling study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2021. The study provided valuable data for understanding the long-term impact of TB. 24. Schoeman J, Wait J, Burger M, et al. conducted a long-term follow-up study on childhood tuberculous meningitis, published in Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology in 2002. The study highlighted the neurological sequelae of TB meningitis in children. 25. Gupta R, Kushwaha S, Thakur R, et al. identified predictors of adverse outcomes in patients with tuberculous meningitis in a multi-center study from India. Published in Indian Journal of Tuberculosis in 2017, the study provided insights into risk factors for poor prognosis. 26. Dhawan SR, Gupta A, Singhi P, et al. conducted a prospective cohort study on predictors of neurological outcomes in childhood tuberculous meningitis in a developing country. Published in Journal of Child Neurology in 2016, the study emphasized the importance of early diagnosis and treatment. 27. Davis AG, Nightingale S, Springer PE, et al. reviewed neurocognitive and functional impairment in adult and pediatric tuberculous meningitis. Published in Wellcome Open Research in 2019, the study highlighted the long-term impact of TB meningitis on quality of life. 28. Dian S, Hermawan R, van Laarhoven A, et al. examined brain MRI findings in relation to clinical characteristics and outcomes of tuberculous meningitis. Published in PLOS One in 2020, the study provided valuable diagnostic insights. 29. Garg RK, Malhotra HS, Kumar N, Uniyal R reviewed vision loss in tuberculous meningitis. Published in Journal of Neurological Sciences in 2017, the study highlighted the ocular complications of TB meningitis. 30. Lam KS, Sham MM, Tam SC, et al. reported on hypopituitarism following childhood tuberculous meningitis. Published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 1993, the study emphasized the endocrine sequelae of TB meningitis.
